newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker chartering rates steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker chartering rates steady to firmer.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rates were steady to firmer in most regions, but slowing trade left West African transatlantic rates slightly weaker, brokers said.
Rates for million barrel vessels moving from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf continued to ease with December requirements mostly covered and demand tailing off.
A cargo booked for Dec 26 loading took W85, off around 2.50 points from Tuesday. Rates for VLCCs going transatlantic were unchanged at W62.5 but chartering activity here was slow too.
North Sea transatlantic trade saw two VLCCs booked by J. Aron, one a 280,000 tonner loading Dec 21 with no rate reported and one 275,000 tonne cargo loading Dec 25 at W62.5.
Brokers said these levels were stable compared with recent trade for 250,000 transatlantic cargoes at W67.5.
Elsewhere Aframax tonnage for inter UK-Cont trips held steady around W100 with Hound Point to Fawley trips valued around W102.50 and cross UKC W97.5.
Active cross-Mediterranean trade continued to support rates for Aframax tonnage at around W105 while Suezmax cargoes traded to Portugal at W92.5 and Turkey at W97.5.

Rates for 250,000 tonne vessels booked from the Middle East to Japan for early January firmed slightly amid active chartering to stand around W63.5. Mideast/Singapore rates for VLCCs were also steadier at W55 but no fixtures were reported.
Mideast/South Korea routes stayed easy with the Astro Alpha booked for 262,000 tonnes on Dec 26 at W49.75 compared with a 250,000 tonne cargo fixed on Tuesday at W54.
Rates for Caribs/upcoast U.S. routes for 70,000 tonne crude cargoes were steady at around W155.
